title: CS2000 Design and Analysis of Algorithms

units.title: Introduction to algorithms
units.question: If an algorithm always returns the right answer, why do we still refuse to call it a solution?

units.title: Asymptotic notation and growth of functions
units.question: If a 100n algorithm beats an n² algorithm only after n = 100, why is the slower-looking one still the one we keep?
units.sourceExcerpt: Module 1 — Asymptotic notation and growth of functions

units.title: Big-O, Ω, and Θ
units.question: If Big-O is already an upper bound, what claim are you making that O(n²) does not make when you write Θ(n²)?

units.title: Analyzing complexity of algorithms
units.question: If almost every array is already nearly sorted, why is the worst-case still the bound we put on the algorithm?

units.title: Recurrence relations
units.question: If T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n already contains the answer, why can't you just read the running time off the code?

units.title: Substitution method
units.question: If the substitution method is a proof, why does it fail until you already know the answer?

units.title: Recursion tree method
units.question: In T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n, every level costs n — so why isn't the total n times infinity?

units.title: Master's theorem
units.question: If the work is always 'root plus children', why does changing the exponent of f(n) flip which term dominates?

units.title: Linear search
units.question: If you are allowed to look at every element, what exactly have you failed to use?

units.title: Insertion sort and selection sort
units.question: Both are Θ(n²) in the worst case — so why does feeding them a nearly-sorted array split their actual work by an order of magnitude?
units.sourceExcerpt: Module 1 — Insertion sort and selection sort

units.title: Bubble sort
units.question: If each pass parks the next-largest element at the end, why is that still Θ(n²) even when the array is already sorted?

units.title: Merge sort
units.question: If you can already sort each half, why is there no free way to zip them back without Θ(n) extra memory?

units.title: Quick sort
units.question: If the two recursive calls do all the sorting, why does a single bad pivot choice turn n log n into n²?

units.title: Strassen's matrix multiplication
units.question: If 7 multiplies beat 8, why does nobody run Strassen on a 4×4?

units.title: Binary search
units.question: You split the range in half — so why is one of the two halves thrown away instead of solved?

units.title: Heap sort
units.question: If a heap already gives you extract-min in log n, why isn't building the heap the expensive part?

units.title: DFS and BFS
units.question: If both only walk unused edges, why does swapping a stack for a queue change which vertices you can claim to have 'found' first?

units.title: Counting sort
units.question: If you never compare two keys, why does the algorithm become slower than comparison sorts as soon as the keys are large integers?

units.title: Greedy strategy
units.question: If each step takes the best available piece, what extra property must the problem have before that is allowed to equal the best overall answer?

units.title: Fractional knapsack
units.question: If value-per-weight is the obvious ranking, why does forbidding the knife (0/1) make that ranking lie?

units.title: Job sequencing with deadlines
units.question: If jobs have deadlines and profits, why does scheduling the most urgent job first fail, and what do you sort on instead?

units.title: Huffman encoding
units.question: If a shorter code exists by dropping the prefix-free rule, why is that shorter code unusable on a stream with no commas?

units.title: Spanning trees
units.question: If extra edges only add cost, why is the minimum connected subgraph forced to be a tree rather than a cheaper DAG?

units.title: Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms
units.question: Both claim the MST. Why does one of them risk adding an edge between two far-away components, and why is that still safe?

units.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
units.question: If a vertex is already marked 'done', what can a later negative edge do that Dijkstra has already forbidden itself from undoing?

units.title: Dynamic programming
units.question: If divide-and-conquer already solves smaller instances, why does recomputing the same subinstance turn an exponential tree into a table?

units.title: 0/1 knapsack
units.question: If you already decided yes/no on item i, why isn't a single running total of value enough — why a row for every leftover capacity?

units.title: Matrix chain multiplication
units.question: Multiplying (A B) C and A (B C) give the same matrix — so why can one parenthesization be a thousand times more arithmetic?

units.title: Longest common subsequence
units.question: If the letters don't have to sit next to each other, why does a single skipped character in the middle force a different table cell, not a restart?

units.title: Bellman-Ford algorithm
units.question: If you relax every edge |V|−1 times, what are you waiting for that Dijkstra refused to wait for?

units.title: Floyd-Warshall algorithm
units.question: If shortest paths can wiggle through any vertices, why does iterating k from 1 to n actually cover every possible internal path, not just the ones that go through k last?

units.title: N-Queens (backtracking)
units.question: If 8 queens have 8⁸ candidate placements, why does refusing a square because of a shared diagonal delete whole subtrees instead of one cell?

units.title: Hamiltonian cycle
units.question: Given a tour, you can verify it in linear time — so why doesn't that give you a polynomial algorithm to produce one?

units.title: Branch and bound (knapsack)
units.question: If you already prune impossible queens, what extra number lets you prune a knapsack branch that is still feasible?

units.title: Rabin-Karp string matching
units.question: If two strings hash to the same number, why is that a maybe-match rather than a match — and why is the rolling hash still worth it?

units.title: Knuth-Morris-Pratt
units.question: After a mismatch at pattern index j, you already know the last j−1 characters of the text. Why does that let you slide the pattern without rereading those characters?

units.title: P and NP
units.question: If a short proof of 'yes' can be checked quickly, why does that not automatically give you a way to find the proof?

units.title: NP-complete
units.question: If SAT and Hamiltonian Cycle look nothing alike, what would a polynomial reduction have to smuggle from one into the other for a SAT algorithm to solve both?

units.title: NP-hard
units.question: Halting is NP-hard and not even in NP. What did we give up when we dropped the requirement that yes-instances have short checkable certificates?
